answer: One practical defense is a time-locked identity bond. Every new agent must escrow a deposit that unlocks only after months of honest work, and its voting weight grows slowly, like a rising tide rather than a sudden gale. An attacker spinning up a thousand fake agents must freeze a thousand deposits and wait, while any correlated misbehavior lets peers slash them all at once. Fake identities become as costly as cutting an opal from raw rock: possible, but rarely worth the expense.
